1	% dog(1) v0.1.0
2	
3	<!-- This is the dog(1) man page, written in Markdown. -->
4	<!-- To generate the roff version, run `just man`, -->
5	<!-- and the man page will appear in the ‘target’ directory. -->
6	
7	
8	NAME
9	====
10	
11	dog — a command-line DNS client
12	
13	
14	SYNOPSIS
15	========
16	
17	`dog [options] [domains...]`
18	
19	**dog** is a command-line DNS client.
20	It has colourful output, supports the DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS protocols, and can emit JSON.
21	
22	
23	EXAMPLES
24	========
25	
26	`dog example.net`
27	: Query the `A` record of a domain using default settings
28	
29	`dog example.net MX`
30	: ...looking up `MX` records instead
31	
32	`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1`
33	: ...using a specific nameserver instead
34	
35	`dog example.net MX @1.1.1.1 -T`
36	: ...using TCP rather than UDP
37	
38	`dog -q example.net -t MX -n 1.1.1.1 -T`
39	: As above, but using explicit arguments
40	
41	
42	QUERY OPTIONS
43	=============
44	
45	`-q`, `--query=HOST`
46	: Host name or domain name to query.
47	
48	`-t`, `--type=TYPE`
49	: Type of the DNS record being queried (`A`, `MX`, `NS`...)
50	
51	`-n`, `--nameserver=ADDR`
52	: Address of the nameserver to send packets to.
53	
54	`--class=CLASS`
55	: Network class of the DNS record being queried (`IN`, `CH`, `HS`)
56	
57	By default, dog will request A records using the system default resolver. At least one domain name must be passed — dog will not automatically query the root nameservers.
58	
59	Query options passed in using a command-line option, such as ‘`--query lookup.dog`’ or ‘`--type MX`’, or as plain arguments, such as ‘`lookup.dog`’ or ‘`MX`’. dog will make an intelligent guess as to what plain arguments mean (`MX` is quite clearly a type), which makes it easier to compose ad-hoc queries quickly. If precision is desired, use the long-form options.
60	
61	If more than one domain, type, nameserver, or class is specified, dog will perform one query for each combination, and display the combined results in a table. For example, passing three type arguments and two domain name arguments will send six requests.
62	
63	DNS traditionally uses port 53 for both TCP and UDP. To use a resolver with a different port, include the port number after a colon (`:`) in the nameserver address.
64	
65	
66	SENDING OPTIONS
67	===============
68	
69	`--edns=SETTING`
70	: Whether to opt in to DNS. This can be ‘`disable`’, ‘`hide`’, or ‘`show`’.
71	
72	`--txid=NUMBER`
73	: Set the transaction ID to a specific value.
74	
75	`-Z=TWEAKS`
76	: Set uncommon protocol-level tweaks.
77	
78	
79	TRANSPORT OPTIONS
80	=================
81	
82	`-U`, `--udp`
83	: Use the DNS protocol over UDP.
84	
85	`-T`, `--tcp`
86	: Use the DNS protocol over TCP.
87	
88	`-S`, `--tls`
89	: Use the DNS-over-TLS protocol.
90	
91	`-H`, `--https`
92	: Use the DNS-over-HTTPS protocol.
93	
94	By default, dog will use the UDP protocol, automatically re-sending the request using TCP if the response indicates that the message is too large for UDP. Passing `--udp` will only use UDP and will fail in this case; passing `--tcp` will use TCP by default.
95	
96	The DNS-over-TLS (DoT) and DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) protocols are available with the `--tls` and `--https` options. Bear in mind that the system default resolver is unlikely to respond to requests using these protocols.
97	
98	Note that if a hostname or domain name is given as a nameserver, rather than an IP address, the resolution of that host is performed by the operating system, _not_ by dog.
99	
100	Unlike the others, the HTTPS transport type requires an entire URL, complete with protocol, domain name, and path.
101	
102	
103	OUTPUT OPTIONS
104	==============
105	
106	`-1`, `--short`
107	: Short mode: display nothing but the first result.
108	
109	`-J`, `--json`
110	: Display the output as JSON.
111	
112	`--color`, `--colour=WHEN`
113	: When to colourise the output. This can be ‘`always`’, ‘`automatic`’, or ‘`never`’.
114	
115	`--seconds`
116	: Do not format durations as hours and minutes; instead, display them as seconds.
117	
118	`--time`
119	: Print how long the response took to arrive.
120	
121	
122	META OPTIONS
123	============
124	
125	`--help`
126	: Displays an overview of the command-line options.
127	
128	`--version`
129	: Displays the version of dog being invoked.
130	
131	
132	ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES
133	=====================
134	
135	dog responds to the following environment variables:
136	
137	## `DOG_DEBUG`
138	
139	Set this to any non-empty value to have dog emit debugging information to standard error. For more in-depth output, set this to the exact string ‘`trace`’.
140	
141	
142	RECORD TYPES
143	============
144	
145	dog understands and can interpret the following record types:
146	
147	`A`
148	: IPv4 addresses
149	
150	`AAAA`
151	: IPv6 addresses
152	
153	`CAA`
154	: permitted certificate authorities
155	
156	`CNAME`
157	: canonical domain aliases
158	
159	`HINFO`
160	: system information and, sometimes, forbidden request explanations
161	
162	`LOC`
163	: location information
164	
165	`MX`
166	: e-mail server addresses
167	
168	`NAPTR`
169	: DDDS rules
170	
171	`NS`
172	: domain name servers
173	
174	`OPT`
175	: extensions to the DNS protocol
176	
177	`PTR`
178	: pointers to canonical names, usually for reverse lookups
179	
180	`SOA`
181	: administrative information about zones
182	
183	`SRV`
184	: IP addresses with port numbers
185	
186	`SSHFP`
187	: SSH key fingerprints
188	
189	`TLSA`
190	: TLS certificates, public keys, and hashes
191	
192	`TXT`
193	: arbitrary textual information
194	
195	When a response DNS packet contains a record of one of these known types, dog will display it in a table containing the type name and a human-readable summary of its contents.
196	
197	Records with a type number that does not map to any known record type will still be displayed. As they cannot be interpreted, their contents will be displayed as a series of numbers instead.
198	
199	dog also contains a list of record type names that it knows the type number of, but is not able to interpret, such as `IXFR` or `ANY` or `AFSDB`. These are acceptable as command-line arguments, meaning you can send an AFSDB request with ‘`dog AFSDB`’. However, their response contents will still be displayed as numbers. They may be supported in future versions of dog.
200	
201	
202	PROTOCOL TWEAKS
203	===============
204	
205	The `-Z` command-line argument can be used one or more times to set some protocol-level options in the DNS queries that get sent. It accepts the following values:
206	
207	`aa`
208	: Sets the `AA` (Authoritative Answers) bit in the query.
209	
210	`ad`
211	: Sets the `AD` (Authentic Data) bit in the query.
212	
213	`bufsize=NUM`
214	: Sets the UDP payload size field in the OPT field in the query. This has no effect if EDNS is diabled.
215	
216	`cd`
217	: Sets the `CD` (Checking Disabled) bit in the query.
218	
219	
220	EXIT STATUSES
221	=============
222	
223	0
224	: If everything goes OK.
225	
226	1
227	: If there was a network, I/O, or TLS error during operation.
228	
229	2
230	: If there is no result from the server when running in short mode. This can be any received server error, not just NXDOMAIN.
231	
232	3
233	: If there was a problem with the command-line arguments.
234	
235	4
236	: If there was a problem obtaining the system nameserver information.
237	
238	
239	AUTHOR
240	======
241	
242	dog is maintained by Benjamin ‘ogham’ Sago.
243	
244	**Website:** `https://dns.lookup.dog/` \
245	**Source code:** `https://github.com/ogham/dog`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""DoT server: TLS-wrapped length-prefixed DNS."""
import socket, ssl, struct, sys, threading, binascii
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
import dnsserver

def handle(conn, mode):
    try:
        while True:
            hdr = conn.recv(2)
            if len(hdr) < 2: return
            (mlen,) = struct.unpack('>H', hdr)
            data = b''
            while len(data) < mlen:
                chunk = conn.recv(mlen - len(data))
                if not chunk: return
                data += chunk
            sys.stderr.write("DOTQUERY: " + binascii.hexlify(data).decode() + "\n")
            sys.stderr.flush()
            resp = dnsserver.build(data, mode)
            if resp is None: return
            conn.sendall(struct.pack('>H', len(resp)) + resp)
    except Exception as e:
        sys.stderr.write("ERR: %r\n" % e)
    finally:
        conn.close()

def serve(port, mode):
    ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
    ctx.load_cert_chain('pki/srv.crt', 'pki/srv.key')
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    sock.bind(('127.0.0.1', port))
    sock.listen(5)
    sys.stderr.write(f"dot listening {port}\n"); sys.stderr.flush()
    while True:
        conn, addr = sock.accept()
        try:
            tls = ctx.wrap_socket(conn, server_side=True)
        except Exception as e:
            sys.stderr.write("TLS ERR: %r\n" % e); sys.stderr.flush()
            continue
        threading.Thread(target=handle, args=(tls, mode), daemon=True).start()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    serve(int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[1])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""DoH server: HTTP/1.1 over TLS, POST application/dns-message."""
import socket, ssl, struct, sys, threading, binascii
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
import dnsserver

RESP_TMPL = b"HTTP/1.1 %s\r\nContent-Type: application/dns-message\r\nContent-Length: %d\r\n\r\n"

def handle(tls, mode):
    try:
        data = b''
        while b'\r\n\r\n' not in data:
            chunk = tls.recv(4096)
            if not chunk: return
            data += chunk
        head, rest = data.split(b'\r\n\r\n', 1)
        sys.stderr.write("REQ: %r\n" % head); sys.stderr.flush()
        clen = 0
        for line in head.split(b'\r\n')[1:]:
            if line.lower().startswith(b'content-length:'):
                clen = int(line.split(b':')[1].strip())
        body = rest
        while len(body) < clen:
            chunk = tls.recv(4096)
            if not chunk: return
            body += chunk
        body = body[:clen]
        sys.stderr.write("DOHQUERY: " + binascii.hexlify(body).decode() + "\n"); sys.stderr.flush()
        if mode == '404':
            tls.sendall(b"HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n")
            return
        resp = dnsserver.build(body, mode if mode != '404' else 'a')
        if resp is None: return
        tls.sendall(RESP_TMPL % (b'200 OK', len(resp)) + resp)
    except Exception as e:
        sys.stderr.write("ERR: %r\n" % e); sys.stderr.flush()
    finally:
        tls.close()

def serve(port, mode, host='127.0.0.2'):
    ctx = ssl.SSLContext(ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER)
    ctx.load_cert_chain('pki/srv2.crt', 'pki/srv2.key')
    sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
    sock.bind((host, port))
    sock.listen(5)
    sys.stderr.write(f"doh listening {host}:{port}\n"); sys.stderr.flush()
    while True:
        conn, addr = sock.accept()
        try:
            tls = ctx.wrap_socket(conn, server_side=True)
        except Exception as e:
            sys.stderr.write("TLS ERR: %r\n" % e); sys.stderr.flush()
            continue
        threading.Thread(target=handle, args=(tls, mode), daemon=True).start()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    serve(int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[1])
